_comment: SYNTHETIC. This is what the UNGROUPED `vulnerabilityFindings` query returns for the `sca`
scope, and it is generated rather than captured: `sca_response.json` beside it is the
GROUPED query -- one row per repository with severity counts -- so it has no per-finding
rows and cannot drive a pipeline.
What is real: the repository branches, their ids and their cloud platforms, all taken from
that captured response. What is synthesised: the findings themselves -- CVEs, packages,
timestamps and exploit signals -- chosen so the confusion matrix has all four quadrants and
an unclassified row, the way brick's own committed response does.
Every finding is CRITICAL or HIGH, matching the `--severities` the tests scan with. A
MEDIUM row here would be a scan returning something it did not ask for, and it made the
severity-filtered `v_lifecycles` disagree with the published OVERALL row -- which is a
real property of the pipeline (OVERALL is computed once over everything scanned) shown
Regenerate rather than hand-edit if the shape needs to change; see
